findings.title: Promotion accepts native receipts without executable binding
findings.why_it_matters: A maintainer can assemble nine syntactically valid native gate receipts that share manifest/run metadata yet never exercised the per-target candidate executables; promote still reaches draft/publish while public archives stay unsmoked on those platforms.
evidence: jq -e --arg id "$(jq -r '.id' <<<"$gate")" ... '.status=="accepted" and .scope=="trusted-candidate" and .gate==$id and .source_sha==$sha and .version==$version and .manifest_sha256==$hash and .run_id==$run' "$path"
docs/release-acceptance.md requires native gate receipts to include binary/archive digests and retained evidence; promote never reads executable_sha256 or binary_sha256 from receipts
scripts/test/test_promotion.sh builds gate receipts with only status/scope/gate/manifest/run_id and no binary fields, illustrating the accepted shape
findings.suggested_fix: In promote.sh, for each gate id matching native/*, require receipt fields (e.g. executable_sha256 or binary_sha256) and jq-compare them to the matching .targets[].executable_sha256 in the verified release-manifest.json before draft/publish.
findings.first_evidence: jq -e --arg id "$(jq -r '.id' <<<"$gate")" ... '.status=="accepted" and .scope=="trusted-candidate" and .gate==$id and .source_sha==$sha and .version==$version and .manifest_sha256==$hash and .run_id==$run' "$path"

findings.title: Native CI green never hashes shipped candidate bytes
findings.why_it_matters: Each native matrix job validates and builds from source on its host, while the published candidate is produced once on ubuntu via GoReleaser cross-compiles; a platform-specific defect in the cross-built artifact can leave native CI fully green and promotion-bound manifest hashes never exercised on that OS.
evidence: "run": "make setup preflight-ci setup-sqlc validate build check-generated check-ci\nmake check-ci-drift"
.github/workflows/release.yml build step: "run": "make release-candidate RELEASE_OUTPUT=\"$RUNNER_TEMP/candidate\"" on ubuntu-24.04 only
.goreleaser.yaml builds use "CGO_ENABLED=0" with goos linux/windows/darwin cross targets, not the per-runner native binary paths
findings.suggested_fix: Treat native matrix success as source-only evidence; bind each native/* gate receipt to release_smoke output that digests the extracted manifest target binary, and fail promotion when that binding is missing.
findings.first_evidence: "run": "make setup preflight-ci setup-sqlc validate build check-generated check-ci\nmake check-ci-drift"

findings.title: Cascade: main CI cancels in-flight candidate CI
findings.why_it_matters: A routine push to main during a release-candidate dispatch shares the Native CI concurrency group with cancel-in-progress=true, aborting the reusable CI child mid-matrix; the candidate run fails or must be restarted, creating retry pressure where operators may skip re-verifying downloaded artifacts.
evidence: release.yml ci job uses workflow_call of ./.github/workflows/ci.yml with the same ref as main pushes
findings.suggested_fix: Give workflow_call invocations a distinct concurrency group (include caller workflow/run_id) or set cancel-in-progress false when github.event_name is workflow_call.

findings.title: Performance gates bind CLI/TUI only to linux amd64
findings.why_it_matters: Promotion recomputes exhaustive CLI/TUI/startup sample matrices against the linux/amd64 executable hash from the manifest; arm64/linux, darwin, and windows shipped binaries receive no analogous automated matrix binding at promote time.
evidence: CLI jq guard uses .manifest.sha256==$hash with that linux_hash; TUI uses .manifest.binary_sha256==$hash
Gate list includes native/linux/arm64, native/darwin/*, native/windows/amd64 without per-target performance report requirements
findings.suggested_fix: Document that only linux/amd64 reference performance is promotion-gated, or add target-scoped performance/report checks for each published GOOS/GOARCH.

findings.title: Silent-pass: minimum job skips check-ci/actionlint
findings.why_it_matters: Hosted Native CI can succeed on the minimum job path without ever running make check-ci; release workflow lint fidelity then depends entirely on all five native matrix runners also completing, not on the minimum job itself.
evidence: Minimum canonical gates run: "make setup preflight-ci setup-sqlc validate build check-generated build-tui\nmake check-ci-drift"
Native canonical gates include check-ci; minimum path does not
scripts/ci-check.sh check runs actionlint on .github/workflows/ci.yml and release.yml
findings.suggested_fix: Add make check-ci to the minimum job canonical gates and update scripts/ci-check.sh contract to match, so actionlint/contract runs on both paths.
findings.first_evidence: Minimum canonical gates run: "make setup preflight-ci setup-sqlc validate build check-generated build-tui\nmake check-ci-drift"

residual_risks: Candidate verification retains GitHub artifact API digest but explicitly does not independently hash the transport ZIP; trust depends on per-member manifest hashes after extraction.

TUI reference measurements run from a clean source checkout at candidate SHA while packaged startup uses the selected binary; divergent overlay/version behavior would not be caught by a single combined bench pass.
Release gate receipts and acceptance records rely on maintainer discipline; automated promotion cannot distinguish physical native execution from hash-bound JSON alone.
testing_gaps: Simulate concurrent main push plus release workflow_call to assert candidate CI is not cancelled or failure surfaces a single actionable retry boundary.
Promotion test should reject native gate receipts that omit executable/binary digests when docs require them.
End-to-end fixture that native matrix build output SHA256 is not assumed equal to manifest target SHA256 unless explicitly extracted from candidate archives.
